podcast.body: During a Prague concert on June 23, 2004, David Bowie attempted to perform this song, but it started and stopped, leading to the entire band leaving the stage. This event was part of a sequence of performances where Bowie was experiencing a heart attack. "And then stationed a station. It started and stopped. And that was it. Everybody left the stage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The title track of the 1976 album, its lyrics introduced the "Thin White Duke" character. This persona was associated with Bowie's gaunt appearance at the time, heavily influenced by his cocaine addiction, which he later claimed made him unable to remember anything about the album's creation. "This was the LP where he introduced the aforementioned Thin White Duke character in the lyrics of Station to Station's title track."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song is mentioned as featuring the "devil's tri tone" (flattened fifth), demonstrating the chord's application across a diverse range of genres beyond heavy metal and jazz, including in the work of prominent rock artists. "In addition to a ton of Sabbath and Hendrix songs, they can also be heard in David Bowie's station to station, the beautiful people by Marilyn Manson, Blurred Girls and Boys, SIGDIS X1 and YYZ by Rush, Enter Sandman from Metallica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
